title: Rigveda 7.72: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.72: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.72 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 538v-539r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.72.1-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 5, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 539r
translation.original_text:
1ā goma̍tā nāsatyā̱ rathe̱nāśvā̍vatā puruśca̱ndreṇa̍ yātam | a̱bhi vā̱ṁ viśvā̍ ni̱yuta̍ḥ sacante spā̱rhayā̍ śri̱yā ta̱nvā̍ śubhā̱nā ||
2ā no̍ de̱vebhi̱r upa̍ yātam a̱rvāk sa̱joṣa̍sā nāsatyā̱ rathe̍na | yu̱vor hi na̍ḥ sa̱khyā pitryā̍ṇi samā̱no bandhu̍r u̱ta tasya̍ vittam ||
3ud u̱ stomā̍so a̱śvino̍r abudhrañ jā̱mi brahmā̍ṇy u̱ṣasa̍ś ca de̱vīḥ | ā̱vivā̍sa̱n roda̍sī̱ dhiṣṇye̱me acchā̱ vipro̱ nāsa̍tyā vivakti ||
4vi ced u̱cchanty a̍śvinā u̱ṣāsa̱ḥ pra vā̱m brahmā̍ṇi kā̱ravo̍ bharante | ū̱rdhvam bhā̱nuṁ sa̍vi̱tā de̱vo a̍śred bṛ̱had a̱gnaya̍ḥ sa̱midhā̍ jarante ||
5ā pa̱ścātā̍n nāsa̱tyā pu̱rastā̱d āśvi̍nā yātam adha̱rād uda̍ktāt | ā vi̱śvata̱ḥ pāñca̍janyena rā̱yā yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
1COME, O Nâsatyas, on your car resplendent, rich in abundant wealth of kine and horses. As harnessed steeds, all our laudations follow you whose forms shine with most delightful beauty.
2Come with the Gods associate, come ye hither to us, Nâsatyas, with your car accordant. 'Twixt you and us there is ancestral friendship and common kin: remember and regard it.
3Awakened are the songs that praise the Aṣvins, the kindred prayers and the Celestial Mornings. Inviting those we long for, Earth and Heaven, the singer calleth these Nâsatyas hither.
4What time the Dawns break forth in light, O Aṣvins, to you the poets offer their devotions. God Savitar hath sent aloft his splendour, and fires sing praises with the kindled fuel.
5Come from the west, come from the east, Nâsatyas, come, Aṣvins, from below and from above us. Bring wealth from all sides for the Fivefold People. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 539r (numbered 60r by the scribe) (OPenn image 539, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 7.72.1 ‹-puru-candreṇa yātam abhi vām›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 539v (numbered 60v by the scribe), begins in RV 7.73.2 ‹-yajate vandate ca aśnītam›. Verses 7.72.1-5 end on this page; 7.72.1 begins on fol. 538v (numbered 59v by the scribe).
